Round 12, the landing round, merged fork main into the round 11 head (a7ef1463f) and built the rulings and the coordinator's decisions in rounds r12a to r12g (item 36): a key written twice in one table refuses the push (tl_note); the scan of record runs at gitleaks' trace level, and gitleaks' own line for a path allowlist's skip on a piece refuses (path_skips), a skip canary checking the running gitleaks' wording (skip_canary, canary_check); each hunk is a piece of its own, a missing final newline is mirrored and the ~ line leads only a piece gitleaks would skip by type (CRED_PIECES_AWK); the feed reads under the clone's diff settings (diff_settings); every pushed merge is read by its first-parent diff too (merge_fp_reads); a path whose diff attribute names a textconv driver refuses (name_reads, attr_reads); and a pushed commit whose encoding label is off a derived list refuses (refuse_commit_encodings). One offer for the whole class with the harness; the offer is authorised and sequenced after the fork landing (the closing paragraph).

The eighth road, stated as executed (the round f5 entry stated it too narrowly, as gitleaks reading its git log FAILURE as an empty scan, and a fix built to that spec would still have failed open): gitleaks 8.30.1 (and 8.28.0, the version CI pins) runs `git -C <root> log -p -U0 <range> --diff-merges=first-parent` itself, and aborts its scan on the FIRST stderr line from that git that is not one it allowlists as a rename-detection warning (by execution: the two rename-detection warnings and the `diff.renameLimit` hint pass; the source names the auto-gc notice too), WHATEVER git's exit status: it logs `ERR [git] <line>` and `ERR error="stderr is not empty"`, drops the rest of the scan, reports the commits it did read as `N commits scanned`, says `no leaks found` for every finding not already emitted, and exits 0. The commit count and byte count it prints may still be the full expected ones (three commits parsed, the noise on the oldest, `3 commits scanned` equal to `git rev-list --count`, a live token in the range, `no leaks found`), so neither git's exit status nor an agreeing commit count distinguishes an aborted scan from a clean one. The hook at f5 classified on the exit status alone (`case $rc in 0) ;;`), so exit 0 read as CLEAN and the credential published, with nothing printed but gitleaks' own lines. The road is open on every clone, the maintainer's included: with the denylist armed, no read of the identifier arm fails in these modes (`git diff-tree` is plumbing and applies no textconv; `git grep` reads the raw blobs), so the f5 entry's sentence that the denylist masked the road was false. Since round r9d the road is closed by construction: gitleaks scans files the hook wrote from the lines the pushed commits add (and, since round r10a, from a merge's binary path read whole from its result blob; since round r11b a third run also reads probe texts of the hook's own beside second copies of the path-scoped pieces; since round r12b3 a fourth run, the skip canary, reads synthetic pieces of the hook's own under a config the hook writes; and since round r12f every pushed merge's first-parent hunks are pieces too) and runs no git (items 33 to 36 below). The executed fault modes, each a REAL push through the installed hook with the denylist armed and a credential assembled at run time, each publishing at the f5 text with zero hook lines:

- a git that writes ONE benign line to stderr and otherwise runs unchanged (a shim on gitleaks' invocation shape; romp-manager's own reproduction): `ERR [git] ...`, `1 commits scanned` of two, `no leaks found`, exit 0; two live credentials published.
- a content-preserving textconv that exits 0 and writes one stderr line (`.gitattributes` `diff=<name>` plus `diff.<name>.textconv`; a personal `core.attributesFile` reaches it too): git log -p exits 0; gitleaks reports the FULL count (1 of 1, 2 of 2, 3 of 3, agreeing with `git rev-list --count` every time), `no leaks found`, exit 0; the token on the remote. This is the mode that defeats a readability probe (`git log -p ... >/dev/null || unscanned` passes: git exited 0) and a count comparison alone.
- a textconv whose converter is missing: git log -p exits 128 (`fatal: cannot exec`), `git diff-tree` exits 0 and `git grep` 1 for the identifier arm; gitleaks `0 commits scanned`, exit 0; published.
- a git that rejects `--diff-merges=first-parent` (any git below 2.31): `ERR [git] error: unknown option`, `0 commits scanned`, exit 0; published, every identifier-arm read succeeding.
- a merge whose side branch the remote already holds, the credential in the plain commit before the merge, the side branch's dropped file's blob unlinked from the store: `git grep` 1, `git ls-tree` 0, `git diff-tree` 0 on both new commits (the merge's combined diff is empty), gitleaks' git log -p 128 (`unable to read`), `1 commits scanned`, exit 0; published. (The f5 entry's shape, the added file's blob gone from the tip's own commit, makes diff-tree exit 128 and the f5 ADDED LINES read refuses first; the shape matters, and this one is the reachable one.)
- a log that comes up short with no stderr line at all (gitleaks' git given `--max-count=1`, the secret in the older of two commits): `1 commits scanned`, `no leaks found`, exit 0; published. No ERR line is written in this mode; only the count condition sees it.
- a git that exits 128 inside gitleaks (`fatal: bad object`), and the f5 entry's fallback shape (a range this clone resolves whose walk then fails): `ERR [git] fatal: ...`, `0 commits scanned`, exit 0; published.
- the controls: two live secrets with a healthy git are refused as a finding (exit 2, both rules named, redacted); git's rename-limit warnings (`diff.renameLimit=1` over twelve renames) are logged at WRN and the finding is still reported, exit 2.
- not executed, by assessment: a transient fault inside gitleaks' own process (a signal, EMFILE) is not reproducible by a separate probe of git and is visible only in gitleaks' own log, which is why the remedy reads that log rather than probing git again.

The fix, in the fold (review round r1; the rule: stop inferring "clean" from exit 0, which says gitleaks reported no finding, not that it scanned; require positive evidence of coverage and refuse without it). The mechanism this paragraph records held from r1 to r9b and was retired in round r9d, when the hook took gitleaks' read into its own (the property paragraph; item 33): the rule stands, and its positive evidence is since then gitleaks' byte figure against the bytes the hook wrote. The hook captures gitleaks' stderr, its log, apart from its stdout (the findings still stream live to the hook's stderr through a third descriptor: `log=$( { "$gl" git ... 2>&1 1>&3; } 3>&2 ) || rc=$?`), re-emits the log, keeps the exit-status arms (1 or above 2: failed_scan and failed_creds as before; 2: a finding), and when gitleaks CLAIMS a scan (exit 0 or 2) applies two independent conditions to an SGR-stripped copy of the log: (1) any line at its ERR level refuses, `the CREDENTIAL scan of <ref> (<sha10>) did not complete: gitleaks logged an error (<the first ERR line>)`, failed_creds=1; (2) the reported `<n> commits scanned.` must equal the hook's own count of the commits with content to scan, `covered <reported> of the <expected> commits with content to scan` on a mismatch, `reported no commit count, so what it read is unknown` when the line is absent, failed_creds=1 on each. Two conditions because either alone has a hole: the short mode writes no ERR line, and an aborted scan can report the whole count; together they hold the scan whole at the granularity of commits and no finer (round 8's refuters: a stream cut inside a commit with nothing on stderr passes both, the property paragraph below). At the r1 text the expected count was derived by a new helper, scannable_commits, over the SAME `git log -p -U0 --format='commit %H' --diff-merges=first-parent` stream by gitleaks' own rule (a commit counts once a file that is neither deleted nor binary has a hunk; gitleaks' sources for v8.30.1 and v8.28.0 read: one `addCommit` per fragment, a fragment one hunk of a non-deleted non-binary file, the count the distinct shas), because `git rev-list --count` over-counts every empty, delete-only, binary-only, mode-only or rename-only commit and every merge with an empty first-parent diff (nine of 22 shapes disagree with gitleaks; that derivation agreed with both gitleaks versions on all 22 and on a 4556-commit range of the fork's own history, 4544 both). The same stream, but not the same bytes: the r1 audit had both reads ask git for a plain stream, `git log --no-color` in scannable_commits and `--no-color` appended to gitleaks' `--log-opts`, because a transform the clone's configuration applies to the stream reaches both readers alike and a count that agrees with an emptied scan is no evidence (the colour road, below). Review round r2 found five more transforms of that stream and replaced the derivation: scannable_commits now reads the OBJECTS and consults no stream (the class paragraph below), and gitleaks' options live in one place, gitleaks_args. The derivation's own failure is its own road, read before the scan: `expected=$(scannable_commits $range) || { rc=$?; expected=""; }` with the clause `the COMMITS of <ref> (<sha10>) could not be counted for the credential scan (a git read exited N)` (`git log exited N` at r1), failed_creds=1; since r6 the read goes through judged_read (gate: the COUNT of commits with content to scan, the same clause with {rc} the status) and its answer is judged as a run of digits, an exit-0 answer of any other shape refused as not a count (the count's awk answering nothing beside a scanner handed a shorter log PASSED at the r5b text, the comparison skipped on the empty count: bats case 185 with the real scanner, red there), as are the repository root (3021 at the r9b text; 2941 at r8c; 2405 at r7b), the range probe (3057; 2977; 2433) and the three reads of the scanner's log (3120, 3125, 3138; 3040, 3045, 3058; 2486, 2491, 2500), each with the scanner's advice on a refusal where the r5b text ended the hook by errexit with no line. The rev-list probe's comment now says what it covers (an UNRESOLVABLE range only; what gitleaks did with the range is read from its log, not its exit status), and the hook's header paragraph states the road, the two-condition remedy and the colour road. The invocation gained that one argument at r1, `--no-color` after `--diff-merges=first-parent` inside `--log-opts` (nine plain-stream options since r2 and ten since r2h, `--root` the tenth, built by gitleaks_args); tests/install-sh.bats's pins on the invocation are substring globs and still match (its stub strips the `--log-opts` value after the range and `--diff-merges=first-parent`), and its stub scanner now reports the range's commit count in gitleaks' own line shape, since the hook requires the count as positive evidence (the harness paragraph). Verified by execution with gitleaks 8.30.1 and 8.28.0, the hook fed its ref line directly and through REAL pushes: the noise mode is refused on both conditions (the ERR line, and `covered 0 of the 2` or `1 of the 2`: the abort's count varies with the race between gitleaks' two readers, and both refuse), the short mode by the count alone (`covered 1 of the 2`), the bad-object and fallback modes by both, the rename warning and the two-secret control still as a finding, the remote unchanged in every refusal; a clean push prints byte-identical output to the f5 text's; on a finding one INF line moves (the log is shown after the live findings). In tests/pre-push-hook.bats, the section "the credential scan's own read: gitleaks' log" (the real scanner, skipped where gitleaks is absent as tests/gitleaks-config.bats skips; the probe tokens assembled at run time; a second generic shim, `git_passing_through <bash test over "$@"> <stderr line or empty> [<appended argument>]`, keyed on gitleaks' invocation shape and no read of the hook's own, with the wrappers gitleaks_git_noisy, gitleaks_git_short and gitleaks_git_warning): the two-secret control, a clean pass with the count shown as before, the no-content shapes (at r1 an empty commit, a deletion, a binary add: four commits by rev-list, `1 commits scanned`, no hook line: a pin on the derivation rule, red on a hook that counted with rev-list; re-cut at r2 for the resolved invocation, under which a binary add and a pure rename count as their bytes say: seven commits, three counted), the ERR mode and the short mode (each red at the f5 text at `[ "$status" -eq 1 ]`: the fail-open), the allowlisted rename warning as a WRN pass control, and the two colour cases (below). Round r3 added, in the same section, the count's two remaining arms with the REAL scanner (a blob the size read cannot find fails the count with the exact clause `a git read exited 3`, where under ROMP_NO_GITLEAKS the count never runs and with the scanner a looser assertion stays green through gitleaks' own ERR arm; an ADDED gitlink whose commit this store lacks passes, counted by both, pinning the `$2 != "160000"` filter of the sizes read, without which the gitlink's absent commit reads `missing` and a clean submodule push is refused; bats cases 46 and 47, red under mutants m10 and m11), and in the showRoot section the one case that holds WHERE the count comes from (round r3's ruling C): a git shim stripping `--root` from every invocation carrying the word `log` and from no diff-tree (git_stripping_root_from_log), log.showRoot false, a credential in the root commit, asserting status 1, `covered 1 of the 2 commits with content to scan` and the key line (case 74); a count derived from an equally hardened `git log -p` stream, the shape round r2's ruling excluded, agrees with the shortened scan and passes it (exit 0, the credential published: mutant m12, red on case 74 alone, where 87 of the 88 cases at 89589e7d3 stayed green on that mutant), since every plain-stream option that neutralises a key for the scanner's git neutralises it for such a count alike, so the thirteen transform cases hold that each named transform is closed and not the derivation; the file's header, the transform section's comment and the count-read case's comment (case 54 since r3, r1's 52: its shim keys on the count read's own shape, `diff-tree --stdin`, not on the derivation) say so since r3.

The property in one sentence: no read the hook itself makes of the pushed objects can fail or come up short in a way the hook cannot tell from an empty result, because each read's status is captured before its output is judged, a non-zero status refuses the push as unscanned, and an exit-0 answer is judged against a fact in hand or is the object's own (the two classes below); there is no read inside gitleaks since round r9d: the credential scan reads the pushed changes itself (list_commits, the listing and its gates shared with the identifier scan; one git diff-tree --stdin over the whole push, the credential feed, each commit's head and tail markers checked in the order fed and the commits read whole counted against the commits fed; the added lines written to pieces of at most 98,304 bytes, each opened by a ~ line until round r12d1, which made each hunk's added lines a piece of their own, as gitleaks' git mode frames a hunk, the ~ line leading only a piece whose leading bytes gitleaks' type check would skip, and a last line followed by git's no-newline notice written without its newline (CRED_PIECES_AWK); since round r10a every line between a commit's two names read, recognized as carrying nothing the feed needs, or routed, and any other refused as a line the feed cannot read (credential_feed); a merge's combined diff applies git's binary verdict whatever --text says, so its Binary files differ notice is routed and the merge's own version of that path read whole from its result blob, pieced as the added lines are (merge_binary_reads, blob_pieces), at the cost that a merge whose binary path's whole blob holds a credential a remote already published refuses the push (its witness the round 10b case in tests/pre-push-hook.bats titled "round 10b (A.2's disclosed cost, with its witness)"); a commit of 64 or more parents refused by name in both scans, since git's combined diff drops or garbles the lines such a merge adds (parent_counts, and the identifier scan's PARENT COUNT); and since round r10b a gitleaks older than 8.25.0, or one whose version answer is not a dotted version, refused where a scan would run (scanner_version); since round r11a the config every run is handed read first by the hook's own reader where a scan would run, a repository config whose rules carry a path condition refused before either run (gitleaks_config); and since round r11c the feed's diff-tree run with diff.suppressBlankEmpty=false (and with GIT_DIFF_OPTS unset until round r12n, whose ruling P has the feed and the first-parent read take the variable as main's git log does, item 37), and parent_counts' rev-list with its output encoding pinned (credential_feed, parent_counts); since round r12a a key written twice in one table of that config refused (tl_note); since round r12d2 the feed given the clone's diff.algorithm, diff.interHunkContext and diff.renames, and since round r12l its diff.submodule, a value it does not read and any diff.<driver>.algorithm refused (diff_settings); gitleaks 8.30.1 and 8.28.0) is now a cut of the hook's own feed, refused naming it (the table's CREDENTIAL FEED row, whose short case is that cut, red at cad898dd2 by publication), where until r9d (afa552298, which retired them) the two arms judging gitleaks' own git log held the scan whole at the granularity of commits and no finer; the coordinator chose this, option (b) (romp-manager, 2026-09-24; confirmed by the repository owner on the landing page, 2026-09-29), and romp-manager's three rulings on the design set its shape (item 33: the five path-scoped rules kept by an additive run whose figure is checked the same way, a merge read by the lines in none of its parents (and since round r12f by its first-parent diff too, item 36) and a rename by its edits, and directory mode, which gives up gitleaks' built-in path exemptions; item 35: a per-rule or targeted path allowlist, in either condition, or a rule's own path, that treats a copy's name differently from the file's path changes that rule's verdict in the copy without skipping it, so the figure agrees, and since round r11b a third run, the probe run, probes each copy's name under the five rules and scans a second copy of each selected piece at its root, refusing when a probe is not named under its rule or a second copy holds a finding;   if (buf != "") line = buf " " line

```bash
  judge = "(^|[^A-Za-z0-9_$.-])grep([ \t)]|$)"
  if (code !~ reads && code !~ judge && code !~ /\[ (! )?-[fx] / && code !~ /done < /) next
  shape = ""
  if (code ~ /2>\/dev\/null|>\/dev\/null 2>&1|\|\| *true|\|\| *:( |$)|\|\| *\{ *[a-z_]+=""/) shape = shape "a:suppressed "
  if (code ~ /=\$\(|="\$\(/ && code !~ /\|\|/ && code !~ /^[ \t]*(if|while|elif) /) shape = shape "b:subst-no-arm "
  if (code ~ /(git|cat|added_lines|stamped_addresses|tag_field|tag_message|chosen_emails|parent_count|scannable_commits)[^|]*\| *(grep|awk|while|cut|sed|sort|tr)/) shape = shape "c:pipe-left "
  if (code ~ /^[ \t]*(if|while|elif|case) / || code ~ /\[ "\$\(/ || code ~ /\) *&& *\[/) shape = shape "d:test "
  if (code ~ /\|\| *rc=\$\?|\|\| *\{ *rc=\$\?|\|\| *return \$\?|\|\| *\{ *[a-z_]*=?"?"?;? *(unscanned|tag_unread|type_unread)|\|\| *\{ *$/) shape = shape "s:status-read "
  if (code ~ reads) shape = shape "R "
  if (code ~ judge && code !~ /git grep/) shape = shape "j "
  if (code ~ /\[ (! )?-[fx] /) shape = shape "f:file-test "
  if (code ~ /done < /) shape = shape "i:input-redirect "
  if (code ~ /^[ \t]*(echo|unscanned) / || code ~ /^[ \t]*\[ "\$rc" -eq 0 \] \|\| unscanned/) shape = shape "p:report-text "
  gsub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line)
  printf "%d\t%s\t%s\n", n, shape, line }
' .githooks/pre-push
```

Command 2 is new in r1, for the WIDENED class: a read that succeeds and hands on LESS than its source holds, with no status to read. One row per statement that can lose part of its input or turn "less" into "absent": a `read` loop with what feeds it (L, with file, herestring or pipe: a final line with no newline comes back from `read` with status 1 and ends a plain `while read` before the body runs; a herestring always ends in a newline, a file or a pipe may not), a command substitution (S: strips every trailing newline and every NUL byte), a parameter expansion that cuts the value (P), a truncating filter (T: head, tail, -n, --max-count, an awk exit, sed -n, cut, sort -u, uniq, tr, grep -v, grep .), a read option that reads less than the object by design (N: -I, -l, -M, -c, --not, --remotes, --diff-merges, -U0, --no-show-signature, --format), a test that treats an empty value as absent (E). The hook's only readers of its own captured text are read, `$(...)`, the parameter expansions and the filters, so listing every statement that has one lists every site of the class; the command cannot see whether a given strip LOSES anything, which is what the table judges. Known false positives, left so the listing is reproducible: L on report lines whose text contains "read " and T on the top-level `exit 1`. Command 1 lists a read loop's CLOSER (`done <`) and command 2 its HEAD (`while read`): the head is the row the f5 method could not see, and the denylist reader's head is where the f5 entry was wrong.

```bash
awk '
{ line = $0
  if (buf != "") line = buf " " line
  if (line ~ /\\$/) { sub(/[ \t]*\\$/, "", line); buf = line; if (!start) start = NR; next }
  n = start ? start : NR; start = 0; buf = ""
  code = line; sub(/^[ \t]*#.*$/, "", code); sub(/[ \t]#[ \t].*$/, "", code)
  if (code ~ /^[ \t]*$/) next
  t = ""
  if (code ~ /(^|[ \t;])read[ \t]/ || code ~ /done <|\| *while/) {
      t = t "L:read-loop "
      if (code ~ /done < /) t = t "L:file "
      if (code ~ /done <<< /) t = t "L:herestring "
      if (code ~ /\| *while/) t = t "L:pipe "
  }
  if (code ~ /\$\(/) t = t "S:subst "
  if (code ~ /\$\{[A-Za-z_!#@*0-9]+(%%|%|##|#|:[0-9])/ || code ~ /^[ \t]*case /) t = t "P:param-trim "
  if (code ~ /(^|[ \t|(])(head|tail|uniq|cut|tr|sort -u|sed -n)([ \t]|$)/ || code ~ /--max-count|-n 1( |$)| -1 | exit[ ;}]/ || code ~ /grep -[a-zA-Z]*v|grep \. /) t = t "T:truncate "
  if (code ~ / -I | -l | -M | -c |--not|--remotes|--diff-merges|-U0|--first-parent|--no-show-signature|--format/) t = t "N:narrow "
  if (code ~ /\[ -[nz] |\$\{#|(^|[ \t;&|])(continue|break)([ \t;]|$)|\|\| *return 0/) t = t "E:empty-test "
  if (t == "") next
  gsub(/^[ \t]+/, "", line)
  printf "%d\t%s\t%s\n", n, t, line }
' .githooks/pre-push
```

The table's figures, by derivation, at the texts the result paragraph after the command names (R=HEAD, and the texts it compares). Since r8b the population is judged by the table's rule and no longer listed by tag: tests/pre-push-reads.tsv holds one row per tool read of the hook, a judged_read tag's row keyed to the tag and an outside row keyed to its read by a fixed substring of the read's command line, each with the fact that shows a whole answer and, since r8b3, after "Its end:" what bounds the answer's END, or the reason an empty or cut-short exit-0 answer there refuses or publishes nothing; the case that drives the read with its tool silent and the case that drives it cut short (or, on a gate= or own= row alone, "none:" and the reason no cut applies), each through a real push; and its class and its end kind. The table case (tests/pre-push-hook.bats 227) is red on a read with no row, a row with no read, a row whose case matches no @test line or pushes through no hook, a short case that asserts no cut, a fact with no end or an end of no known kind, since round r8c an outside row whose short column is none: with a reason (an outside row names its short case, because a cut of a read made for the report can change what the report says), since round r9b a case or a short case whose title does not carry `: <read>:`, the case of another read (the trailing colon refusing a read whose name is a prefix of a neighbour's), and a header block that differs from the output of tests/pre-push-reads-header.sh by a byte, read since round r9b from the first BEGIN marker alone, so a doubled or inserted marker line is no longer dropped before the comparison. The command below, run from the repo root, derives the figures from the committed files (R the text read, B the r7b text for the change of tags):

```bash
R=HEAD B=1185a7e43
T=$(git show "$R:tests/pre-push-reads.tsv"); H=$(git show "$R:.githooks/pre-push")
rows() { awk -F'\t' '$1 ~ /^(gate|own|outside)$/' <<< "$T"; }
count() { sort | uniq -c | sort -k1,1nr -k2 | awk '{ printf "%s %s; ", $2, $1 }'; echo; }
echo "rows by kind: $(awk -F'\t' '!/^#/ && NF { print $1 }' <<< "$T" | count)"
echo "prose by paragraph: $(awk -F'\t' '$1 == "prose" { print $2 }' <<< "$T" | count)"
echo "classes: $(rows | cut -f6 | count)"
echo "end kinds: $(rows | cut -f8 | count)"
echo "facts stating an end: $(rows | cut -f3 | grep -c 'Its end: ')"
echo "silent cases: $(rows | cut -f4 | sort -u | wc -l) distinct for $(rows | wc -l) rows"
echo "short cases: $(rows | cut -f7 | grep -v '^none: ' | sort -u | wc -l) distinct; none: $(rows | awk -F'\t' '$7 ~ /^none: / { print $1 }' | count)"
for col in 4 7; do rows | cut -f"$col" | grep -v '^none: ' | while IFS= read -r ref; do
  n=$(git show "$R:tests/pre-push-${ref%%:*}.bats" | grep -F -- "${ref#*:}" | grep -c '^@test ')
  [ "$n" -eq 1 ] || echo "column $col: $ref matches $n @test lines"; done; done
echo "facts recording a round 8b3 publication: $(rows | cut -f3 | grep -c 'round 8b3: .*publish')"
echo "tags: gate= $(grep -c 'judged_read gate="' <<< "$H") call sites, $(grep -oE 'judged_read gate="[^"]*"' <<< "$H" | sort -u | wc -l) names; own= $(grep -c 'judged_read own="' <<< "$H"), $(grep -oE 'judged_read own="[^"]*"' <<< "$H" | sort -u | wc -l)"
diff <(git show "$B:.githooks/pre-push" | grep -oE 'judged_read (gate|own)="[^"]*"' | sort -u) <(grep -oE 'judged_read (gate|own)="[^"]*"' <<< "$H" | sort -u) | sed -n 's/^\([<>]\) judged_read /  \1 /p'
echo "hook $(wc -l <<< "$H") lines, block $(awk '/^# BEGIN generated block/ { p = 1; next } /^# END generated block/ { p = 0 } p' <<< "$H" | wc -l); cases: $(for f in pre-push-hook pre-push-identity pre-push-message install-sh; do printf '%s ' "$(git show "$R:tests/$f.bats" | grep -c '^@test ')"; done)"
```

The denylist's bytes and the split's cost (the audit's A and B; both hold, built): build 4 stripped judged_read -k's marker, and split the denylist's capture into lines, by removing patterns in the pusher's locale, and under a UTF-8 locale bash 5.2.21 answers other bytes, and another length, when it removes a pattern from a text that starts with a lead byte followed by a backslash, which is not valid UTF-8 (C3 5C or E9 5C: 22 bytes stripped to 6, their content changing from run to run), so a denylist whose first line starts so refused every push as read short, and the split read any line that starts so as other bytes, which can publish a push adding that line's bytes (with the strip in the C locale, build 4's split published one such push in one of two runs, gate4-repair-m-patsplit-bash5.log); and the split copied the capture's remainder at each line, 108 s for a 20,000-entry denylist in the C locale and past 300 s under C.UTF-8, where d2091c2c1's loop took 0.68 s and 0.73 s (gate4-repair-parse.log). Built: strip_keep_marker removes the marker in the C locale for every -k read (the DENYLIST, the SYMLINK TARGET of a link at the tip, the CHOSEN ADDRESSES); and the read builtin splits the capture, LC_ALL=C IFS=<newline> read -r -d '' -a over a pipe from printf '%s\0' of the hook's own shell, as a command substitution reads, at each newline byte whatever the locale and with no globbing, in 1.08 s and 1.16 s for the 20,000 entries and 28 s for one line of 1,000,000 bytes, as the loop's 28 s (the trim's cost); a read that does not reach the NUL printf ends the capture with (a pipe cut short, a redirection that failed) refuses naming the split; each line is then trimmed as the loop trimmed it, in the pusher's locale, so an entry edged by a Unicode space is trimmed as before. Two other splits give the same entries for all 810 files below in all three locales and were this repair's first texts: mapfile -t over the same pipe, which tests/shell-portability.bats refuses as bash 4 (its case 7 went red, gate4-repair-mapfile-shell-portability-*.log), and the shell's word splitting with IFS a newline, which sets IFS outside a read, which the guard's census (case 704) names (run with that split, the census refuses it while the new cases pass, gate4-repair-m-ifssplit-*.log). Over 810 files (10 written by hand and 800 fuzzed over newline, CR, space, tab, #, a, b, z, 01, 7F, E9, C3, A9, backslash, *, VT, ?, [, ], U+2028, U+00A0 and the Shift-JIS pairs 95 5C and 83 5C), the repaired parse in the C locale gives d2091c2c1's loop's entries for all 810, and under C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8 it gives, for 809, the entries of a model that splits at each newline byte and trims a line that is valid UTF-8 of Unicode white space and any other line of ASCII white space; in the other, bash's trim reorders the bytes of a line that is not UTF-8, and d2091c2c1's loop gives the same bytes, as the comment above the read says. The audit's premise that d2091c2c1's loop read the file byte for byte in any locale does not hold, and the difference was a hole of its own (pre-existing, fail-open): under a UTF-8 locale bash's read took a newline that follows a lead byte into the line, with the next line, so a comment line ending in a Latin-1 letter (E9) took the entry after it, and a denylist with no other entry left the identifier scan off: through a real push under C.UTF-8 at d2091c2c1 the commit adding that entry PUBLISHED (the Latin-1 comment's case, red there; gate4-repair-rb-d209-new-*.log), and over the corpus the loop under C.UTF-8 differs from the repair on 67 of the 810 files. THE LOCALE CLASS (the ruling's A; the audit's H2 and the re-check's F2, subsuming F3): the hook body runs under LC_ALL=C as a whole, exported once as the first body statement right after bash_gate's call and before any text tool or parameter-expansion pattern operation of the body, so every grep, awk, sed, trim and comparison reads the bytes the push carries whatever the pusher's locale. The code ahead of the gate stays bash-3.2-safe and runs no text tool; its pattern operations (the walk up the denylist's path, the split of ROMP_HOOK_BASHES and of a candidate's version answer, lookup_answer's match) run in the pusher's locale and split at the ASCII bytes /, : and the space, which no UTF-8, EUC, GBK, GB18030, Big5 or Shift_JIS character holds (the export paragraph; build 5's text had claimed a C locale of the walk's own, the audit's LOC-5 and T4). The cost, stated in the export paragraph and pinned by three witness cases (the cases titled the C locale's cost, the audit's LOC-1): the denylist's case-insensitive matching folds ASCII letters alone, so an entry with a letter outside ASCII matches its exact bytes and a line naming it in capitals publishes; an entry's edges lose ASCII whitespace alone to the trim, so an entry edged by an ideographic space is grepped with it and a line holding the bare string publishes (a cost the coordinator did not accept: build 6 trims a set of Unicode spaces, part (23)); and the chosen addresses compare the same way, so an address that differs from a chosen one in the case of a letter outside ASCII is refused, the strict side. The first two publish what d2091c2c1 refused for a pusher in a UTF-8 locale and the third refuses what it published; each case is red at d2091c2c1. The trim's cost is a second consequence of the ruled whole-body locale beside the folding the ruling named, put to the coordinator with the repair. THE COLOUR ROAD, the ninth, of the widened class, on two statements of the r1 text (523 scannable_commits and 598 the gitleaks invocation; on the r2 text the derivation at 569-583 and the invocation at 674, on the r2c text 749-763 and 853, on the r2e text 778-792 and 885), FIXED in r1 by the round's audit and, as the first found instance of the class the next paragraph states, closed structurally in r2; no OPEN row remains on the committed text. The fault: a stream that holds less than the objects, read alike by both readers, so the "independent" count agrees with the emptied scan. With `color.ui=always` or `color.diff=always` in any config scope git reads (the clone's, or a user's global gitconfig, which reaches gitleaks' git the same way), git colours `log -p` written to a pipe. gitleaks 8.30.1 and 8.28.0 find no file header in the SGR-prefixed stream, report `0 commits scanned` and `no leaks found`, write no ERR line (git wrote nothing to stderr) and exit 0; the fixer's scannable_commits read the same coloured stream and its `^diff --git ` and `^@@` patterns missed the same lines, so expected 0 equalled reported 0, both conditions passed, and the hook exited 0. By execution: the control refuses as a finding on every text; with either key set, a REAL push through the installed hook, the denylist armed, published a branch carrying two live credentials assembled at run time with nothing printed but gitleaks' two INF lines, at the f5 text and at the fixer's r1 text alike. gitleaks scanning nothing under colour is pre-existing (every text before r1 passes there too); what r1's first text added was a count condition derived from the same `git log -p` stream, which therefore shared every upstream transform with the scan it checked: a count derived from the same stream is independent of the scanner's PARSING, not of the stream's TRANSFORMS. The fix, the smallest edit on both statements: `git log --no-color -p -U0 ...` in scannable_commits, so the derivation reads a stream it has cleaned itself, and `--log-opts="$range --diff-merges=first-parent --no-color"` on the gitleaks invocation, so the scanner's git is given the same (an option on the log outranks color.diff=always in every scope). The first alone was tried and is not enough: the secrets push is refused `covered 0 of the 2` (fail-closed) but a CLEAN push under colour is refused too (`covered 0 of the 1`: gitleaks still scans nothing), so both reads get the option. The `--log-opts` form rather than a `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` prefix on the invocation (also verified to work): tests/git-hermetic.bash exports `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=5` with five pairs for every bats run, and a prefix of 2 would override them for gitleaks' git. Comments at the three sites say why: one sentence in the hook's header paragraph, a paragraph at the end of scannable_commits' comment, two lines in the invocation's comment. Two bats cases at the end of the gitleaks section of tests/pre-push-hook.bats: a credential under `color.ui=always` is refused as a FINDING (the coloured stream shown by execution first, then the hook: status 1, `2 commits scanned`, the github-pat rule named, `gitleaks found a credential`, and not the incomplete-scan line), and a clean push under `color.diff=always` passes with `1 commits scanned` and no hook line, so the counts agree for the right reason. Fails-before: against the f5 text the file runs 1..50 with 41 ok and 9 not ok (the fixer's seven, plus 49 at `[ "$status" -eq 1 ]`, the fail-open, and 50 at `1 commits scanned`, since gitleaks reported 0 there); against the fixer's r1 text 48 ok and 2 not ok (49 and 50 at the same assertions). So case 50 is not a bare pass control: it pins that gitleaks reads the commit under colour, the scanner-side half of the repair. The real-push probe with the committed hook, gitleaks 8.30.1 and 8.28.0: the control refused as a finding; the noise mode refused on both clauses; the short mode by the count alone (`1 of the 2`); the fail mode on both; the rename warning refused as a finding on the secrets branch and passing on the clean one; a clean push exit 0 with 0 hook lines; under `color.ui=always` and under `color.diff=always` the secrets branch refused as a FINDING (`2 commits scanned`, `leaks found: 2`) and the clean push passing (`1 commits scanned`); the remote holding main alone after every run. The identifier arm is unaffected (its tip grep has `--no-color` since r1, diff-tree since f5, and ls-tree, cat-file, rev-list, config and `log --format` print no colour, as check-attr -z and `cat-file blob` since r2c, and the read-list grep with `--no-color`, the numstats with -z and a merge's combined patch with `--no-color`, the same read as added_lines, since r3 to r3d; all five hit kinds named under `color.ui=always`). THE CLASS BEHIND THE COLOUR ROAD, transforms of a stream both readers shared, found by review round r2 and closed structurally in the same round (2026-09-21). The mechanism below held until round r9d, which retired the count and gitleaks' own git read with it (item 33): since r9d the credential feed is plumbing given every option explicitly and gitleaks reads only the bytes the hook wrote, so no transform of a stream reaches either. The r1 fix gave the hook two coverage conditions so one failing could not hide the other, and its own audit found they were not independent under colour and patched that with `--no-color`. Round r2 found five more transforms of the same `git log -p` stream on the committed r1 text, each by execution: a `.gitattributes` `diff=<driver>` entry with a hiding `diff.<driver>.textconv`, and a `-diff` attribute on the file carrying the credential, each rewrote or emptied the patch for gitleaks AND for the hook's count, so both conditions passed and a REAL push through the installed hook published a live credential assembled at run time with zero hook lines; `format.pretty` set to a non-default format and `log.date` set to relative each broke gitleaks' header parse while its content coverage stayed whole, so a CLEAN push was refused `covered 0 of the 1` with advice pointing at disabling the scan; and `log.showSignature=true` with an unverifiable signature wrote gpg's report into the stream (the refuters' runner: the f5 text published, the r1 text refused clean pushes). Six transforms in two rounds, three of which published a credential while the hook reported clean and three of which refused clean pushes, from one mechanism: a count derived from the stream it checks is only as independent as the stream is clean, and patching transforms one at a time keeps finding roads (romp-manager's ruling for the round, section A: a wrong mechanism, not a missing case). The fix takes the count off the stream: scannable_commits reads the OBJECTS, `git rev-list --parents` over the range (every commit gitleaks' log walks, each with its first parent), one `git diff-tree --stdin -r --raw --no-renames --root` over those pairs (each commit's changed paths against its first parent, a root against the empty tree, with their blob shas, applying no attribute, driver or colour) and one `git cat-file --batch-check` over the added and type-changed blobs; a commit has content when one entry that is not a deletion gives the patch a hunk: a gitlink whose sha changed (a `Subproject commit` line either way), a modified blob whose sha changed (a mode-only change keeps the sha and prints no hunk; a file emptied prints one), or a new or type-changed path whose blob is not empty (an empty new file or link prints no hunk); a blob cat-file cannot find exits 3 with a fatal line and refuses, and any of the three reads failing refuses at the caller (`a git read exited N`), never counting 0. The plain-stream options are hardening, not the fix: gitleaks_args builds gitleaks' argument list in ONE place, which the hook's invocation and tests/pre-push-hook.bats's scan_direct (which evals the function out of the hook file) both call, so the two match by construction; its `--log-opts` value carries the range, `--diff-merges=first-parent` and nine options at r2, ten since r2h, each outranking the config key it neutralises in every scope: `--no-color`, `--no-textconv`, `--text` (a -diff attribute or core.bigFileThreshold makes git call a file binary and print no hunk for it; under the option gitleaks scans what git would call binary, and the derivation counts every changed non-empty blob, binary or not), `--no-renames` (a pure rename is a deletion and an addition for both reads), `--submodule=short` and `--ignore-submodules=none` (diff.submodule and diff.ignoreSubmodules otherwise drop a gitlink hunk from gitleaks' stream and refuse a clean push), `--no-show-signature`, `--pretty=medium` and `--date=default`, and since r2h `--root` (log.showRoot, below); three of the nine r2 options (`--no-renames` and the two submodule options) are the round's fixer's additions beyond the ruling's list, each a false-refusal remedy recorded in the round's log with its alternative. Verified by execution: the hook's own scannable_commits and gitleaks_args, read out of the hook file, against gitleaks 8.30.1 and 8.28.0 over 40 commit shapes (round r1's 22, with the binary-only and rename-only commits now counted by all three; eleven typechange and gitlink shapes; files with and without a trailing newline; a replace ref with and without the export) and over the fork's own HEAD~300..HEAD range at 3a05b63bb, the round 2 commit's parent and the round 2 fixer's staged-tree base (300 first-parent steps; 4513 commits by rev-list; 4502 with content on all three counts, the derivation and both versions; the figures derived here once and referred to from the count read's row above and from the body: re-derived in round r6c from the committed hook's scannable_commits over 3a05b63bb~300..3a05b63bb, `git rev-list --count` 4513, `--first-parent` 300, the derivation 4502 in 0.8 s, and gitleaks 8.30.1 and 8.28.0 each reporting `4502 commits scanned` and `no leaks found` under gitleaks_args' log options, in 59 s each), 0 mismatches; 36 diff- and log-affecting config keys swept, every one passing through under the final option set (two, diff.submodule and diff.ignoreSubmodules, needed the two submodule options); the derivation takes 0.8 s over that range where the r1 patch read took 44 s, and gitleaks itself 55 s under `--text --no-renames` where it took 45 s, a push faster overall. `log.showRoot` set to false, which hides a root commit's diff from gitleaks' log while the derivation counts the root's entries, was named at r2 and r2c as a fail-closed over-refusal rather than a road (a push carrying a root commit refused `covered N-1 of the N commits with content to scan`, the r1 text having published a credential in a root commit under the key; since r2c one line after the coverage line naming the key and the remedy) on the premise that no option turns the root's diff back on. The premise was false: round r2e found by execution that `--root` outranks the key (`git log -p --root` under the key set false prints the root's hunk, two hunks with the option and one without, under git 2.43.0 and both gitleaks versions), so romp-manager's ruling of 2026-09-21 15:52Z, which on that premise had reversed the refusal to an environment override (a GIT_CONFIG_COUNT pair setting the key true for the hook's child gits, staged in r2e with a refusal arm for a scanner whose git does not inherit it), was replaced in round r2h by the fold owner with the option itself (rulings-r2h.md, flagged for romp-manager's confirmation in round 3; the pair is recoverable from the r2e fixer log). NEUTRALISED: `--root` is the tenth option in gitleaks_args' `--log-opts`, the shape `--pretty` and `--date` take, and it outranks the key in every scope and travels on the scanner's command line, so a root commit's diff is scanned (its credential found as a finding), a clean root push passes with the scanner's count the hook's own, and a scanner git that does not inherit the hook's environment still reads it. REFUSES: a scanner whose git does not honour the option, or any other count that comes up short, is refused on the count as before, and when the short count meets the key false in the clone's configuration (showroot_configured, the file value read once at the top of the hook) and a root commit in the range, the refusal also names the key, says the scanner's git did not honour the `--root` option the hook passes on its log, and gives the remedy (set the key to true or unset it and push again, or `ROMP_NO_GITLEAKS=1` for that one push). The ruling's reason (romp-manager's, restated by the fold owner for the option): fail-closed is the fallback for what the hook cannot see, not the answer when it can neutralise the cause; a refusal a contributor must fix by editing their own git config, for something the hook could have ignored, is a false refusal; the key belongs in the hardening list beside format.pretty and log.date; and the option is the narrowest mechanism, one word on one command line, where the pair injected configuration into every git the hook runs. Beyond the replacement switch the hook exports nothing for the gits it runs (a caller's GIT_CONFIG pairs pass through untouched, a negative pin). The two halves of the hook differ in KIND, stated at its header: since r9d the credential feed is plumbing given each option explicitly, since r11c with diff.suppressBlankEmpty=false pinned on its command line (ruling C, extra5-1; GIT_DIFF_OPTS was unset there too until round r12n, whose ruling P has the feed read it as main's git log does, item 37), since r12d2 given the clone's diff.algorithm, diff.interHunkContext and diff.renames and since r12l its diff.submodule (diff_settings; diff-tree reads diff.renameLimit and diff.indentHeuristic itself, as git log does), and gitleaks reads only the bytes the hook wrote (from r2 to r9b the credential half's own count was derived from the objects and no configuration touched it, while the scanner inside it read a log stream); the identifier half reads a log and diff stream, so it is config-dependent by construction. What can hide a blob from its two content reads is closed since r3 by a DERIVED PROPERTY rather than key by key: git's own verdict on each read against the blob's bytes (refuse_hidden_paths: git produced no hunk for a blob that is text), which covers the diff attribute, core.bigFileThreshold, a driver under any name and a rule a later git adds with one mechanism and no enumeration to keep current, in a one-parent commit's diff and in a merge's combined patch alike. That sentence is what keeps the next key from reopening this entry, and the enumeration that failed is why it is the sentence: at r2c the half was hardened by an enumeration of attribute values (round r2c's attribute road closed by `unset`, a binary-true driver and the two reserved words that do not hide), and round r3 found the size key and check-attr's reserved words outside it by real pushes, the same class round r2 had ruled on for the credential half (a guard keyed on a name, a spelling or a value rather than on the property), so the entry keys on the effect and not on the cause. Beside the class, the premise the whole hook rests on is stated at the hook's header and enforced: both scans read the objects at the pushed shas on the premise that what they read is what the push transfers; a replace ref breaks it (every read followed the substitute while the push transferred the original, and a real push published a banned string and a credential at the pushed sha with both scans reading clean), so `GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS=1` is exported beside `set -euo pipefail` for every git the hook runs (gitleaks' own included until r9d; it runs none since), and refuse_replace_refs, run before either scan, refuses the push under any `refs/replace/` ref (or under the namespace `GIT_REPLACE_REF_BASE` names), naming each ref and the premise: a scan under replacement cannot vouch for the bytes pushed. At the r2 text the refusal was unconditional (a clone with no denylist and no gitleaks was refused too when it carried one), the ruling's text taken and the alternative (refuse only when a scan is armed) recorded in the round's log; round r2c ruled for the alternative and NARROWED the gate: refuse_replace_refs lists the replace refs only when identifier_scan_armed (the denylist file exists, at ROMP_PRIVATE_STRINGS or the XDG default, through private_strings_file) or credential_scan_armed (ROMP_NO_GITLEAKS unset and a gitleaks binary resolving through ROMP_GITLEAKS or PATH and executable, through gitleaks_binary) holds, the two predicates scan_identifiers' and scan_credentials' own early returns read, so the gate and the scans agree by construction, and the predicates decide only whether a scan runs (an empty denylist arms a scan that greps for nothing; a skipped or absent scanner keeps its silence or its notice). The reason, the ruling's: the refusal prevents a false CLEAN REPORT, and where no scan runs there is no report and nothing false to prevent, so a clone that never asked for either scan stays unaffected, as CLAUDE.md promises (the identifier scan a no-op on an absent denylist; gitleaks absent a loud notice and no scan). THE IDENTIFIER SCAN'S OWN INSTANCE OF THE CLASS, the identifier half of boundary B2, found open by the r2 audit by execution, closed in round r2c by refusal rather than by scanning, found OPEN AGAIN by review round r3 (2026-09-21) by execution, the r2c closure having been keyed on an enumeration, and closed since r3 by a DERIVED PROPERTY, git's own verdict on each read, its scope made equal to the property's by rounds r3c to r3f (2026-09-22). Both content reads of the identifier arm read what git calls TEXT: the tip's `git grep -I` skips a blob git calls binary and the per-commit `diff-tree -p` prints no line for one. At r2c the entry, the hook's header and CLAUDE.md enumerated how git calls a blob binary (its bytes, a NUL in the first 8000; or its PATH's diff attribute, a `-diff` line or the `binary` macro in .gitattributes, .git/info/attributes or the file core.attributesFile names, or a driver whose `diff.<driver>.binary` is true), and refuse_hidden_paths read check-attr's VALUE for every regular file at the tip and in each new commit (`unset` hides, a driver hides when its binary key reads true, `set` and `unspecified` do not), so a text file under such an attribute was refused rather than read, and a REAL push through the installed hook had published a synthetic denylist string in one at the r2 text. Round r3 found two ways past that enumeration, each reproduced by real pushes with the denylist armed and gitleaks reporting clean, independently by both refuters and again by the round's fixer: core.bigFileThreshold, a third way git calls a blob binary, in the diff and not in the grep (the hook's own credential half names the key and neutralises it with `--text`; the identifier half had not carried it across), so a text blob over the key printed `Binary files ... differ` in the per-commit read while check-attr answered `unspecified` and the check passed it; and a diff driver NAMED `set` or `unspecified`, with `diff.<driver>.binary` true, for which check-attr answers exactly that word, which the value arm read as no attribute. The ruling (rulings-r3, section A): judge by GIT'S OWN VERDICT, do not neutralise a key and do not parse a value; a `-c core.bigFileThreshold=<large>` on the per-commit read was rejected as a third per-key patch on a privacy surface after two rounds had found the same class, a `--text` on that read was rejected by execution (it reverses the documented binary-by-bytes pass), and the corrections a size-reading route needed (strictly greater than the effective threshold; the unset key falling back to git's built-in default and not to 0; its own cat-file read) were all corrections to reasoning about the cause, the signal to key on the effect; the finding's own fix for the reserved words (reading diff.<value>.binary for them) was rejected too, since it falsely refuses a clean push where `unspecified` is also the answer for a path with no attribute. THE MECHANISM as committed (rounds r3 to r3f, every read of it through judged_read since r6; refuse_hidden_paths, with the helpers as_lines, numstat_rows and combined_rows, and since r6 the joins as named functions the helper runs whole, tip_unlisted_read_file, tip_blobs, tip_candidates, merge_rename_candidates, unlisted_verdict_path, join_candidates and byte_counts, and since r7 nul_records, the shell's count of the rows a join appended): the per-commit half is judged by git's own verdict on the read the scan makes. The population is every non-deleted post-image whose object is a BLOB (a regular file or a symlink, modes 100644, 100755 and 120000; a gitlink names a commit), a type change judged as its new object (the diff prints it as a deletion and an addition judged alone: a numstat of the empty tree against the commit's tree for that path, the tree's name from git hash-object; pinned since r5 by cases 102 and 103, the new link GONE at the tip, where the r3g cases kept it at the tip and the tip-owns rule decided them), less a post-image whose blob equals every pre-image blob (a mode-only change: the diff prints its mode lines with no hunk and no Binary line, so it hid nothing new, while the pair's stat calls an unchanged blob over the key or holding a NUL binary; pinned since r5 by case 106, the change with the file GONE at the tip through a real push, since case 105 keeps the blob at the tip where the tip-owns rule decides it: the property is the blob's absence from the pushed tip, not the file's), and less a blob the pushed TIP's tree holds under any path, which the tip half judges (read by its grep or its symlink pass, or refused as hidden there), so the per-commit road covers only content ABSENT from the tip, the intermediate-commit shape, which bounds the exposure. For a commit with ONE parent, `git diff-tree --numstat` over the pair the per-commit diff reads (-M): a post-image git reports as binary, a dash for each count, is one the diff printed no hunk for, the same decision on the same two blobs (they agree on every blob with bytes; an empty blob under such a rule is the one pair the numstat calls binary while the diff prints its header alone, a candidate here that passes as empty); a PURE rename, which the diff prints nothing for, is judged as the addition of its new path by a second numstat (--no-renames), the rule the r2e rename refusal set, so the explicit diff line the advice names lifts it for the new path (cases 90 and 93: the remedy passes; a file under -diff renamed to a plain path AND changed in the same commit is refused, the diff having judged the pair by the path it came from and printed no hunk; the tip holds the renamed blob in case 90, so the tip-owns rule decides it there, and the exception itself is pinned since r5 by cases 91 and 92, the lifted rename with the new path GONE at the tip passing and its twin with no later diff line for the new path refused, red under m-rename-exception: the property pinned is the blob's absence from the pushed tip, not the file's). For a MERGE, the combined patch itself (`git diff-tree -p -r -M -c --root --no-commit-id --no-color`, the read added_lines makes, byte for byte between the commit's sha lines that added_lines asks for with --always since r8 and a second --stdin line since r8b3), read again and parsed section by section (combined_rows, the header's path C-unquoted as git quotes it): a section printing `Binary files differ` is a path the patch printed no hunk for, a candidate; a section with a hunk was read; a path with the header alone is a candidate judged by its bytes (an added empty file passes as empty; a non-empty blob so printed would be refused as hidden, an arm no shape found reaches, since a header-only section for a blob with bytes is a mode change over content some parent holds); a path with no section whose blob some parent holds under a path the merge lacks is a pure rename, judged as the addition of its new path by the empty-tree numstat, the candidates read from the merge's deletions against EACH parent (`diff-tree --raw -m`, since the combined listing names a deletion only when every parent held the path); a path with no section that is no rename is a verdict the read owed and did not print, refused as unscanned. The combined patch judges by a rule of its own that no per-parent verdict reproduces: it applies no size rule, and it applies a path's diff attribute to a symlink as the pairwise diff does not, which is why r3d replaced the per-parent numstat approximation for merges (r3's disclosed excess, a merge's own change to a file over the key refused as hidden while the patch had printed its hunk, went with it). The tip half likewise derives the set git's grep treats as binary from git's own report: the same `git grep -I`, asked to list the non-empty files it READ (`-l -z -e ''`), the complement over the tree's regular files with bytes (`ls-tree -r -z -l`) being the files it skipped; a symlink's target is read whole by the symlink pass, by cat-file, whatever any attribute or key says. No attribute value is parsed anywhere for a decision: check-attr is read once per REFUSED path for the report's label alone (`diff.<value>.binary` looked up first for every answer, since a driver may be named `set`, `unspecified` or `unset`; then `unset` names the -diff line or macro; any other answer names no attribute, and the line states the blob's size and the clone's core.bigFileThreshold as facts a reader needs and not as a cause, or, for a one-parent commit's changed file whose previous version is binary by its bytes, that cause, the key's facts beside it where the key is set), and a check-attr that fails, answers about another path or answers nothing changes the words and never the verdict (since r5b the tail as well: a failed read says the attribute could not be read and that whether an attribute of its path accounts for the verdict is unknown, both facts kept and both remedies printed, where the r5 text asserted after a failed read what the read could not establish). Two SCOPE constraints, the ruling's, both by execution: per-commit ONLY, since `git grep -I` on the tip is unaffected by the size key and a tip-side size or binary rule would be a FALSE refusal (case 97: a big text file carrying the string AT the tip under the key is a HIT by the tip grep, which reads it, and the tip is never called hidden); and an explicit `diff` attribute keeps outranking the key, in the grep and in the diff alike, which still prints the hunk under the key, so it is a hit and never a refusal (case 96), and it is the remedy the advice names.
